experiment_description: Central concept: construct a parameter-free, materials-specific model for magnetic flux noise in superconducting devices by computing the disordered exchange-interaction landscape of paramagnetic O2 adsorbates on an Al-terminated sapphire (0001) surface, rather than assuming a statistical distribution of spin couplings. Density-functional-theory calculations are performed with VASP using a 500 eV plane-wave cutoff, PAW pseudopotentials, and the vdW-DF-cx van der Waals functional. The simulated structure is a pair of nearest-neighbor O2 molecules adsorbed on top of an Al-terminated three-layer (0001) Al2O3 slab passivated by H on the opposite side. The periodic slab is six surface units wide in both in-plane directions, with dimensions 28.70 Å × 24.86 Å, a 14.5 Å vacuum gap, 796 total atoms, and Gamma-point sampling. Atomic forces are relaxed to 0.005 eV/Å. Each O2 molecule carries two unpaired spins. Six stable O2 binding orientations on the surface are labeled 0 through 5; nearest-neighbor relative orientations are denoted [a,b], where a and b identify the orientations of the two molecules. Spin-pair total energies are computed by initializing the O2 pair in ferromagnetic UUUU and antiferromagnetic UUDD spin configurations using VASP MAGMOM and relaxing while preserving the initialized spin configuration. In any formula result, J([a,b]) is defined as E_UUUU([a,b]) − E_UUDD([a,b]) in meV for a nearest-neighbor O2 pair with relative orientation [a,b]. Spin anisotropy is computed for one equilibrium-bound O2 molecule by constraining the two unpaired spins perpendicular or parallel to the O2 molecular bond axis. The spatial scope is the full DFT supercell containing one nearest-neighbor O2 pair embedded in the periodic Al2O3 surface slab; the orientational scope is all twenty symmetry-distinct nearest-neighbor O2-pair orientations used to parameterize the later Monte Carlo spin lattice.

isolated_o2_binding_energy_orientations_.description: The DFT binding energy of an isolated O2 molecule in the lower-energy threefold-degenerate surface-orientation set.
The DFT binding energy of an isolated O2 molecule in the higher-energy threefold-degenerate surface-orientation set.

o2_orientation_energy_splitting_meV.description: The energy separation between the two threefold-degenerate sets of stable O2 adsorption orientations on Al2O3 (0001).

spin_anisotropy_coefficient_meV.description: The coefficient multiplying |O_i · s_i| in the single-molecule O2 spin-anisotropy energy on the Al2O3 (0001) surface.

nearest_neighbor_exchange_energy_lookup_.description: The DFT nearest-neighbor spin-exchange energy function for O2-pair relative orientations on Al2O3 (0001).

minimum_exchange_energy_meV.description: The most ferromagnetic value in the DFT nearest-neighbor O2-pair exchange-energy set.

maximum_exchange_energy_meV.description: The most antiferromagnetic value in the DFT nearest-neighbor O2-pair exchange-energy set.

smallest_absolute_exchange_energy_meV.description: The smallest absolute magnitude in the DFT nearest-neighbor O2-pair exchange-energy set.

experiment_description: Central concept: use the DFT-derived, orientation-dependent O2 exchange landscape to simulate a disordered adsorbate monolayer and the XY-like spin correlations responsible for superconducting-loop flux noise. A 20 × 20 periodic lattice of O2 adsorption sites is placed on the Al-terminated Al2O3 (0001) surface with lattice spacing l = 4.8 Å. For full coverage, the lattice contains 400 O2 molecules and each occupied site has six nearest neighbors. O2 orientational configurations are sampled by a Metropolis Monte Carlo simulation using the O2-lattice Hamiltonian H_O2lattice = sum_i [E_i^b(O_i) + (1/2) sum_j=NN F(O_i,O_j,r_i-r_j)], with DFT-derived isolated binding energies and nearest-neighbor orientation-pair energies. The O2-orientation Monte Carlo begins at 10^5 times the target temperature, cools smoothly for 10^6 steps to the target temperature, and then runs for another 10^6 steps. The quenched O2 disorder is represented at a target temperature of 0.01 K. Spin configurations on the resulting O2-orientation landscapes are sampled using the spin Hamiltonian H_spin = sum_i [E_anisotropy(O_i,s_i) − (−g_s mu_B s_i/hbar)·H_ext + (1/2) sum_j=NN J(O_i,O_j,r_i-r_j)(s_i·s_j/2)], where E_anisotropy(O_i,s_i)=0.037 meV × |O_i·s_i| and J is the DFT exchange lookup for the local O2 pair orientation. Spin Monte Carlo uses a combination of Metropolis and Wolff cluster updates, with one Wolff update per nine Metropolis steps. For each parameter set, 8 spin Monte Carlo simulations are run for each of 12 independently generated O2-orientation configurations, giving 96 spin simulations. At zero applied external magnetic field and no applied electric field, spin-spin correlation functions are computed across the full 20 × 20 periodic lattice as a function of spin-spin separation up to the finite-size limit, over a temperature sweep spanning the plotted low-temperature BKT regime. The correlation function C(r) is fit to (|r−r'|/l)^−eta, where r and r' are spin positions, l is the 4.8 Å lattice spacing, and eta is the algebraic scaling exponent. The BKT transition is identified by eta = 1/4; the effective exchange scale is inferred from eta = kT/(2π|J_eff|), where k is the Boltzmann constant and T is temperature.

zero_field_bkt_transition_temperature_mK.description: The BKT transition temperature extracted from the algebraic spin-spin correlation scaling of the full-coverage O2 spin lattice at zero applied fields.

zero_field_effective_exchange_energy_meV.description: The effective exchange-energy scale inferred from the fitted BKT correlation exponent for the disordered full-coverage O2 spin lattice at zero applied fields.

experiment_description: Central concept: propagate the materials-specific O2 spin lattice in time to predict magnetic flux noise in a superconducting loop without fitting an assumed disorder distribution. Initial spin configurations are taken from the 96 spin Monte Carlo configurations generated for each parameter set on 20 × 20 periodic O2 lattices with 50%, 75%, or 100% O2 coverage. Dynamics are integrated using the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation dM/dt = −[gamma/(1+alpha^2)] M×H_eff − [alpha gamma/(1+alpha^2)] M×(M×H_eff), with H_eff = −(1/mu_0) delta H_spin/delta M. The numerical integrator is Runge-Kutta-Fehlberg RKF45 with adaptive timestep initialized at 4 fs, near-zero damping alpha = 1e-8, and a 100 ns trajectory length per simulation. The total spin trajectory over the full 20 × 20 lattice is Fourier transformed to obtain magnetic-noise spectra. The measurement configuration uses zero applied magnetic field, zero applied electric field, and O2 spin-lattice temperature 0.01 K. Flux noise through a representative SQUID loop is obtained from the simulated spin fluctuation spectral density using the analytic magnetic-moment-to-flux conversion for a superconducting film loop with loop radius R = 12 µm and line width W = 0.5 µm. Frequency spectra are evaluated over the simulated dynamic bandwidth shown for MHz-to-hundreds-of-GHz frequencies; the reported low-frequency flux magnitudes are evaluated at 10 MHz for the defined SQUID geometry.

flux_noise_10MHz_100pct_coverage_phi0_pe.description: The calculated magnetic flux-noise amplitude through the defined SQUID loop for a full monolayer of O2 adsorbates at 10 MHz and zero applied fields.

flux_noise_10MHz_75pct_coverage_phi0_per.description: The calculated magnetic flux-noise amplitude through the defined SQUID loop for 75% O2 coverage at 10 MHz and zero applied fields.

flux_noise_10MHz_50pct_coverage_phi0_per.description: The calculated magnetic flux-noise amplitude through the defined SQUID loop for 50% O2 coverage at 10 MHz and zero applied fields.

zero_field_frequency_noise_exponent_rang.description: The fitted power-law exponent range n for magnetic flux-noise spectra proportional to 1/f^n in the specified low- and high-frequency windows for O2 coverages from 50% to 100%.

spin_wave_resonance_frequency_range_GHz.description: The frequency interval containing the magnetic resonance in the simulated zero-field spin-noise spectrum.

experiment_description: Central concept: test whether the same materials-specific O2-on-Al2O3 spin model produces the temperature dependence and susceptibility-flux-noise cross-correlation expected for ferromagnetic spin domains contributing to superconducting-device flux noise. For the temperature-dependent flux-noise calculation, full-coverage O2 spin lattices on a 20 × 20 periodic Al2O3 (0001) adsorption grid are sampled by the same orientation Monte Carlo, spin Monte Carlo, and LLG procedures as described for the zero-field spectra. The applied magnetic field and applied electric field are both zero. The LLG trajectories use RKF45 integration, 4 fs initial adaptive timestep, damping alpha = 1e-8, and 100 ns trajectory length. The flux-noise spectral power is evaluated at 160 MHz over a spin-temperature sweep from 0.01 K through and above the sub-kelvin spin-correlation regime. For susceptibility-noise cross-correlation, the same full-lattice magnetization trajectories are used, and the dimensionless marker is SMχ''/(SM Sχ''), where SM is the magnetization noise power and χ'' is the imaginary part of the magnetic susceptibility inferred proportional to the magnetization noise power; the simulated cross-correlation is averaged over frequencies between 1.5 MHz and 2.5 MHz for temperatures from 0.01 K to 2.0 K. The spatial scope is the full simulated periodic spin lattice and the statistical scope is the ensemble of 96 spin trajectories per parameter set.

flux_noise_change_factor_160MHz_0p01K_to.description: The approximate multiplicative increase in simulated magnetic flux-noise power at 160 MHz across the specified low-temperature interval.

flux_noise_temperature_of_reported_turno.description: The spin temperature at which the reported simulated 160 MHz flux-noise trend changes from increasing with temperature to decreasing at higher temperature.

magnetization_susceptibility_cross_corre.description: The qualitative temperature dependence of the simulated magnetization-susceptibility cross-correlation over the specified temperature interval.

experiment_description: Central concept: determine whether an external static magnetic field suppresses magnetic flux noise from the materials-specific disordered O2 spin system by polarizing the paramagnetic adsorbate spins. The simulated sample is a full-coverage O2 monolayer on a 20 × 20 periodic Al-terminated Al2O3 (0001) adsorption lattice, parameterized by DFT exchange energies and O2 spin anisotropy. O2 orientations are generated by Metropolis Monte Carlo and spins are initialized by the combined Metropolis/Wolff spin Monte Carlo procedure. For each field value, LLG dynamics are propagated with RKF45 integration, an initial adaptive timestep of 4 fs, damping alpha = 1e-8, and 100 ns trajectory length, using 96 starting spin configurations per parameter set. The temperature is fixed at 0.1 K, the applied electric field is zero, and the static magnetic field is swept from zero into the sub-tesla range shown for the comparison, with reported suppression evaluated at 0.01 T and 0.1 T. The dependent variable is the magnetic flux-noise power at 100 MHz obtained from the full-lattice spin trajectories; suppression factors are normalized to the zero-magnetic-field value under otherwise identical simulation conditions.

flux_noise_reduction_factor_100MHz_0p01T.description: The factor by which the simulated 100 MHz magnetic flux noise is reduced at the specified static magnetic field relative to zero field.

flux_noise_reduction_factor_100MHz_0p1T.description: The factor by which the simulated 100 MHz magnetic flux noise is reduced at the specified static magnetic field relative to zero field.

experiment_description: Central concept: establish the microscopic electric-field coupling mechanism by computing how the charge distribution and electric dipole moment of a nearest-neighbor O2 adsorbate pair depend on whether its two-molecule spin configuration is ferromagnetic or antiferromagnetic. The DFT setup is the same VASP/PAW/vdW-DF-cx Al-terminated Al2O3 (0001) slab calculation used for the exchange energies: 500 eV plane-wave cutoff, three-layer Al2O3 slab passivated with H on the opposite side, 28.70 Å × 24.86 Å in-plane periodic supercell, 14.5 Å vacuum, 796 atoms, Gamma-point sampling, and relaxation to 0.005 eV/Å. Twenty symmetry-distinct nearest-neighbor O2 relative orientations [a,b] are evaluated. For each orientation pair, ferromagnetic UUUU and antiferromagnetic UUDD spin states are relaxed, and the in-plane electric dipole moment difference is computed. In any formula result, p([a,b])=(p_x,p_y) is defined as (P_UUUU^x − P_UUDD^x, P_UUUU^y − P_UUDD^y) in eÅ for the nearest-neighbor O2 pair with relative orientation [a,b]. The spatial scope of each dipole calculation is one O2 nearest-neighbor pair in the full periodic surface slab; the orientational scope is the complete twenty-orientation lookup table used to add the electric-field term E·p to the spin-pair energy splitting in later simulations.

spin_state_dipole_difference_lookup_eA.description: The DFT in-plane electric dipole moment difference vector between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic spin states for each nearest-neighbor O2-pair relative orientation.

maximum_spin_state_dipole_difference_mag.description: The largest magnitude of the in-plane electric dipole moment difference across the nearest-neighbor O2-pair orientation set.

average_spin_state_dipole_difference_mag.description: The average magnitude of the in-plane electric dipole moment difference across the nearest-neighbor O2-pair orientation set.

experiment_description: Central concept: use the DFT-computed spin-dependent O2-pair dipoles to test electric-field tuning of the exchange landscape, BKT transition, and magnetic flux noise in the disordered paramagnetic adsorbate layer. The simulated sample is a full-coverage O2 monolayer on a 20 × 20 periodic Al-terminated Al2O3 (0001) adsorption lattice with 400 occupied sites and six nearest neighbors per site. O2 orientation disorder is generated by the Metropolis O2-lattice Monte Carlo recipe, and spins are sampled using the combined Metropolis/Wolff spin Monte Carlo recipe. The spin Hamiltonian includes the DFT exchange lookup, O2 anisotropy E_anisotropy=0.037 meV × |O_i·s_i|, and an additional electric-field contribution E·p to the UUUU–UUDD pair-energy splitting, where p is the DFT dipole-difference vector for the local nearest-neighbor O2 relative orientation. The applied electric field magnitude is 10^7 V/cm, the applied magnetic field is zero, and full-lattice spin-spin correlation functions are computed over the 20 × 20 periodic lattice for temperatures spanning 0.01 K to 5.0 K and spin-spin separations up to the finite-size limit. Correlations are fit to (|r−r'|/l)^−eta with l = 4.8 Å; eta = 1/4 defines the BKT transition. For flux noise, LLG trajectories are propagated from the electric-field-modified spin configurations with RKF45 integration, 4 fs initial adaptive timestep, damping alpha = 1e-8, and 100 ns trajectory length. The flux conversion uses the same representative SQUID loop geometry with radius R = 12 µm and line width W = 0.5 µm, and the reported flux amplitude is evaluated at 10 MHz.

electric_field_bkt_transition_temperatur.description: The BKT transition temperature extracted from algebraic spin-spin correlation scaling under the specified applied electric field.

electric_field_flux_noise_10MHz_100pct_c.description: The calculated magnetic flux-noise amplitude through the defined SQUID loop under the specified applied electric field at 10 MHz.

electric_field_low_frequency_noise_expon.description: The fitted exponent n for low-frequency magnetic flux noise proportional to 1/f^n below 100 MHz under the specified applied electric field.
